title: FAA narrows the first rollout of its AI airspace-routing adviser
friendlyTitle: The FAA will start small with an AI tool for flight routes
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration will initially use its SMART system to suggest alternative routes for flights around Washington-area airports. Following airline concerns about the scope, the 90-day test will feed advice through existing procedures rather than create new controller or airline processes.
friendlySummary: A new AI system will suggest other routes around three Washington-area airports. Air traffic controllers will keep using their normal procedures during the first 90-day test.
whyItMatters: A limited advisory rollout is a useful pattern for introducing AI into safety-critical infrastructure: preserve existing authority, measure the system in a bounded setting and expand only after operational evidence. Travellers could eventually see fewer weather and congestion delays if it works.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Starting with advice instead of automatic control reduces risk. If the test works, it could later help prevent some flight delays.
